title: Attics, Crawl Spaces and Tight Spaces (course overview video)

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Building attic access hatch with a ladder below; Danny at the base with a headlamp and a radio. Medium shot. Lower third: Danny Smith, Operations Manager.
scenes.on_screen: Attics, Crawl Spaces and Tight Spaces
scenes.says: Sooner or later a fixture, a junction box or a run of cable puts you in an attic, a crawl space or some other tight spot. These are places where it's hard to see, hard to move and hard to get out fast. This course is about planning for that before you go in, so nothing in there catches you off guard.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Inside a hot attic: insulation, dust in the air from a work light. Danny voice-over.
scenes.says: First, the conditions. Attics get hot, and heat wears you down faster than you expect. Insulation and dust irritate your skin, eyes and lungs. You'll learn how to dress for it, what protection to wear, how to pace the work, and when it's time to come out and cool down. Bring water, and tell your partner how long you expect to be up there.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Close-up: work boots stepping only on joists; a board laid across joists as a walkway.
scenes.on_screen: Step only on joists or a walk board. Never on the ceiling between them.
scenes.says: Second, footing. Between the joists is usually just the ceiling below, and it won't hold you. You'll learn to keep your weight on framing or a proper walk board, and to watch for nails, wiring and other things you can trip over or hit your head on.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Crawl space entrance with a work light set inside; a partner outside with a radio.
scenes.on_screen: Light the space | Keep in contact | Know your way out
scenes.says: Third, light, communication and getting out. You'll learn to light the space properly, keep in contact with someone outside, and know your way out before you need it. If something goes wrong, you want to be able to get out quickly, and you want someone to know where you are.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Danny at the crawl space entrance, medium close-up.
scenes.on_screen: Space might need a permit? STOP and call.
scenes.says: Fourth, and this is the big one. Some spaces need a permit before anyone goes in, because the air or the conditions can hurt you. You'll learn the signs of a space like that. If you think you're looking at one, you don't go in. You stop and call your supervisor.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Danny at the attic hatch, medium shot.
scenes.says: Plan the space before you plan the fixture. Know how you're getting in, what's in there, how you're getting out, and who knows you're in there. Now start the first lesson, and take each quiz as you go.
